clue.text: A former pop group's enthralling album

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the band's name holds the album inside it

parts.note: A-ha were a Norwegian pop band of the 1980s
an LP (long-player) is an album

explanation.surface: A one-time pop band releases a record that captivates its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' looks like an article but is the definition. A-ha were the 1980s Norwegian band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter that begins its alphabet corresponds to our letter A.

clue.text: Sir is happy — Carol is unhappy

definitions.note: Sir abbreviates Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), a book of the Apocrypha; the clue reads as 'Sir is [of the Apocrypha]'

indicators.note: a word that is unhappy is out of sorts, so the letters of the two preceding words are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight is cheerful while a woman named Carol is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir' is not a knight but the standard abbreviation for Sirach, also called Ecclesiasticus, which is in the Apocrypha. 'is unhappy' tells you to rearrange HAPPY CAROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirach is one of the books Protestant Bibles set apart as of doubtful authority, outside the accepted canon.

clue.text: Independent setter cut off by one playing a nutty game

parts.note: Phi is one of the regular setters of the Independent crossword
to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are frolicking about, so the word one is rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper puzzle-maker is interrupted by someone at play in an odd game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges ONE to OEN. Philopoena is an old parlour game played with twin-kernelled nuts, which makes 'nutty' literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Philopoena is a game in which two people share a double almond kernel and the loser of a forfeit pays a gift.

clue.text: Matching beer bottles imitate kegs initially

indicators.note: to bottle is to enclose, so the beer word holds the following letters inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words imitate and kegs

explanation.surface: Bottled beer that copies the taste of draught from kegs.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are matching are the same, or similar, in appearance.

clue.text: An eye open showing separate parts?

parts.note: a private eye is a detective, and DI stands for Detective Inspector
something out in the open is visible, there to be seen

explanation.surface: An eye that opens shows its separate components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye' is crossword slang for a detective; here a DI, a Detective Inspector, not the letter I. 'showing' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being split into distinct portions is described as divisible; the question mark marks the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Macbeth's victim is able to, after torment

indicators.note: after places the word for 'is able to' following the word for torment

parts.note: to dun is to pester persistently, especially for a debt
can means is able to

explanation.surface: Someone becomes capable of something once they have been tormented.
explanation.walkthrough: DUN, to harass someone repeatedly for payment, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Scottish king is murdered in his sleep by his host in the play.

clue.text: Lovely nuts Mr Sullivan smashed up?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the preceding word are scrambled

parts.note: Ed Sullivan was the American television variety host

explanation.surface: A lovely but crazy Mr Sullivan has wrecked something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' turns LOVELY into VOLLEY; Ed Sullivan hosted a famous US TV show. In tennis a smash hit high is a kind of volley, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball struck before it bounces has been volleyed; a smash at the net is such a shot, struck from above.

clue.text: Sort of car crime I cover up — um…

indicators.note: to cover is to wrap round, so the crime word and I enclose what follows

parts.note: a sin is a crime or wrongdoing
taken as written
um and erm are both hesitation noises

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly admits hushing up a car crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of 'cover up' but is fodder: SIN plus I cover UP plus ERM.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermini is a small hatchback, a class of compact family car.

clue.text: Worker perhaps following dispute

parts.note: a worker bee is an example of a worker
F is the abbreviation for following, as in ff in a book

explanation.surface: A labourer starts a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a grievance or quarrel.

clue.text: It's regularly seen on games console close to cable

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter, here of the word seen

parts.note: the DS is a Nintendo handheld games console

explanation.surface: A cable plugged into a games console is regularly visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to cable' looks like the last letter of 'cable' but is the definition: telegrams (cables) were signed off with an end marker.
explanation.definitionFit: In telegraphy, the end signal marks the finish of a cabled message.

clue.text: Old leg — one leg, mind

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
I is the Roman numeral one
leg or on is the cricket term for the side of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: An elderly person with one leg left minds things.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Your mind is your view or belief, as in 'to my mind'.

clue.text: See what's said when one pair feeds information

indicators.note: one thing feeds another when put into it, so the following pieces go inside the information word

parts.note: a lead is a piece of information or a clue
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sees what's being said when a couple passes on a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand speech by watching the movement of the speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Jade and iron ore transported around island's port

indicators.note: around tells you that the rearranged letters are placed around the island abbreviation
transported means moved, so the letters of jade and iron ore are moved into a new order

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Jade and iron ore are shipped round an island's harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges JADE IRON ORE, which then goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil's second city is a major Atlantic harbour.

clue.text: Measure uniform, and I'd cut dress adornment

indicators.note: the following two pieces cut into the dress adornment, splitting it

parts.note: a flounce is a wide ornamental frill on a skirt or dress
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone measures a uniform and plans to cut a decoration from a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluid ounce is a unit of liquid volume.

clue.text: Bending my rod, shoal of simple marine life

indicators.note: bending distorts, so the letters of my rod and shoal are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: My fishing rod bends as I hook a shoal of simple sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrosomal relates to the hydrosome, the body of a hydrozoan colony such as a polyp.

clue.text: Supply lines for opening of military exercise

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of military

parts.note: PT stands for physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A soldier gets lines for a military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre prompter feeds forgotten lines to actors.

clue.text: Spanish beach where sand may be turned to be effective

parts.note: playa is Spanish for beach

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word for where sand may be is read backwards

parts.note: a sand trap, or bunker, on a golf course holds sand

explanation.surface: A Spanish beach where sand is turned over to good effect.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf course's sand trap gives TRAP; 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part is to contribute or have an influence on an outcome.

clue.text: Turn in, say, taking a friend as a friend

indicators.note: turn means turn round, so the letters of the words in and say are read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) means say
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone turns in, taking a companion along as a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn in' looks like going to bed. 'Turn' reverses IN plus EG, giving GENI.
explanation.definitionFit: Genially means in a friendly, cordial manner.

clue.text: What chaps assume gives us wrong answer

parts.note: us is British colloquial for me, as in 'give us a hand'

indicators.note: wrong means mistaken, so the letters of answer are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone gives us the wrong answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'give us' often means 'give me', so 'us' gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's wear is the clothing that men put on.

clue.text: Princess, a little light, given strength

parts.note: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a small light

explanation.surface: A princess with a small torch is given power.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealed metal or glass has been toughened by heating and slow cooling.

clue.text: Mayfair inhabitant's not very clever? More so!

parts.note: Mayfair's postcode is W1, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: not means without, so the word for very is removed from the inhabitant word

parts.note: a liver is one who lives somewhere, an inhabitant

explanation.surface: A Mayfair resident is not very bright, or brighter still.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a wealthy London district with the postcode W1. LIVER loses V for very.
explanation.definitionFit: More wily means cleverer, more cunning.

clue.text: Spike is a friend, one setter admits

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the setter word lets in the friend word

parts.note: the setter is me, from the setter's own view
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Spike is a friend, as one compiler confesses.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce through with a stake.

clue.text: Stingy old man neglected our mission

parts.note: pa is father, an old man

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disorder, so the letters of our mission are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mean old man neglected our task.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimonious means mean and miserly with money.

clue.text: Famous, but only a reporter?

definitions.meaning: a reporter is not an editor, so the phrase breaks up as not plus ed, the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone famous, but merely a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as NOT ED: a reporter is not an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous means celebrated; one merely reporting is not the editor.

clue.text: Bomb causing swell around lake

indicators.note: around places the swell word around the lake abbreviation

parts.note: a swell is a dandy, a fop

explanation.surface: A bomb causing a swell around the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a failure, as is a bomb in show business.

clue.text: Bargain veg shows standard's dropped

indicators.note: dropped means removed, so the standard word is taken from the vegetable

parts.note: a parsnip is a root vegetable
par is a standard level

explanation.surface: A bargain vegetable stall shows standards dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a British colloquial term for something cheap.

clue.text: Story about last to feature in horse race

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story word goes around the rest

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: in places the final letter of feature inside the horse word

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: last to means take the final letter of feature

explanation.surface: Tale about last to feature in a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse race' looks like one item; 'horse' is NAG and 'race' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Race in the sense of descent: ancestry or a family line.

clue.text: Not a word meaning "many"- not "varied"

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of many and not are rearranged

explanation.surface: Not a term for many, not a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: An opposite is a word whose sense is the contrary of another.

clue.text: Secretary's safe — that is somewhere to keep stationery

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
peter is old criminal slang for a safe
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A secretary's safe is where to keep stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is thieves' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A papeterie is a box or case for writing materials.

clue.text: Lodge with hollow walls

indicators.note: the hollow word walls in, encloses, the with abbreviation

parts.note: a dell is a small hollow

explanation.surface: A lodge with hollow walls.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to reside there.
